articles.name: Parameters are missing in an API Order Status use case
articles.title: Parameters are missing in an API Order Status use case
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

When using an API Order Status use case, some parameter values may appear in the API call configuration but fail to populate during the conversation. In some cases, only one parameter is collected while the remaining required values are missing, which prevents the order status workflow from triggering correctly.

Resolution steps

A common cause is that multiple API integrations were created for the same Order Status check. If one of those integrations requires more parameters than the bot collects in the Order Status use case, the workflow may fail and only some values may populate. Misconfigured or missing API parameters can also contribute to the issue.

To resolve the issue:

  • Review the API integrations configured for the same Order Status check
  • Remove any duplicate API integration that is conflicting with the intended setup
  • Confirm that the remaining API integration includes the correct required parameters
  • Verify that the bot is collecting every parameter needed by the Order Status use case
  • Test the flow again to confirm that all parameter values populate and the API triggers successfully

If the issue was caused by a duplicate integration requiring additional parameters, deleting that duplicate integration should allow the correct values to populate as expected.

To learn more API integrations in AI agents, see About the integration builder for AI agents.

articles.name: Announcing the ability to convert existing tickets to service catalog requests
articles.title: Announcing the ability to convert existing tickets to service catalog requests
articles.body:
Zendesk is pleased to announce that agents and business rules can associate existing tickets with service catalog items.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

Previously, service request forms were used only when a user submitted the request through the service catalog. Tickets created through other channels, such as email or messaging, couldn't be converted to service requests without a manual workaround.

Now, the Service ticket field, which is visible on all tickets associated with a brand that has the service catalog turned on, can be used to directly associate a ticket received through other channels with a service catalog item. When a value is specified for the service field, the ticket automatically changes to use that service's request form and fields. Similar to changing between ticket forms, values in fields shared by the ticket form and the service request form are retained. Any required fields on the service request form must contain values before they can submit the ticket.

A ticket's service field value can be set manually or automatically with triggers and automations. See Converting tickets to service requests.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Zendesk understands that many requests begin through a general intake form or other channels before a user knows which service is needed. For example, an employee might email their IT team about a network problem or submit a general IT request only for the agent to determine they need a service catalog item that requires certain information.

This change supports triage workflows without requiring agents to recreate the request or manually select and populate an alternative ticket form. It also lets admins classify incoming tickets automatically with business rules, reducing the effort required to accurately identify service requests received through other channels.

What do I need to do?

This change is being rolled out to all accounts with access to the service catalog. Train your agents on how to convert tickets to service requests and vice versa. Optionally, admins can also create or edit triggers and automations to automatically convert incoming tickets to service requests.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Converting tickets to service requests
articles.title: Converting tickets to service requests
articles.body:
When the service catalog is turned on for a brand, agents can convert tickets into service requests when they are associated with a service catalog item. When a service is set for a ticket, the ticket's form, fields, and requirements are updated to the applicable service request form. This allows agents to convert requests received through other channels, such as email or web form, into service requests.

What's my plan?
All Suites Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus

When the service catalog is turned on for a brand, agents can convert tickets into service requests when they are associated with a service catalog item. When a service is set for a ticket, the ticket's form, fields, and requirements are updated to the applicable service request form. This allows agents to convert requests received through other channels, such as email or web form, into service requests.

This article contains the following topics:
  • Considerations when converting tickets to service requests
  • Converting tickets to service requests
  • Converting a service request to a ticket
Related articles:
  • Adding services to your service catalog
  • Submitting service catalog requests

Considerations when converting tickets to service requests

All tickets associated with brand that has a service catalog turned on include a Service ticket field. Requests submitted through the service catalog are automatically created with a service request form, but requests submitted through other channels use ticket forms by default. Adding a value to a ticket's service field, either manually or with a business rule, converts a ticket to a service request.

When the ticket form changes to a service request form associated with the selected service, the following things happen:
  • The ticket displays the fields configured for the selected service.
  • Values are retained for fields that are present on both forms.
  • Required fields on the service request form must be completed before the ticket can be saved.

A service request can be converted to a ticket by removing the value in the service field.

You can't convert closed requests from tickets to service requests or vice versa.

Converting tickets to service requests

Tickets are converted to service requests by adding a value to the ticket's service field. This can be done automatically, with triggers, or manually by agents. See:
  • Automatically adding a service to a ticket
  • Manually adding a service to a ticket

Automatically adding a service to a ticket

To use triggers to automatically add a service to a ticket, use the Service > Service action.

To automatically add a service to a ticket
  1. Create or edit a ticket trigger.
  2. Under Conditions, specify one or more qualifications the ticket must meet to be converted to a service request.
  3. Under Actions, click Add action and select: Service > Service | Service catalog item, where Service catalog item is replaced with a service from your service catalog.

    The the service specified in the action statement's Value field is the value that is added to the ticket's Service field.

Manually adding a service to a ticket

If an agent is working a ticket and determines it needs to be converted to a service request, they can manually add the service to the ticket as long as it has a status of new, open, pending, or on-hold.

To manually add a service to a ticket
  1. In Support, access a ticket.
  2. In the ticket properties panel, under Service, select the service being requested in the ticket.
  3. Review the fields on the service request form to ensure all required fields contain values.
  4. Save your change by clicking Submit as and selecting the appropriate status.

Converting a service request to a ticket

Deselecting a service from a ticket's service field removes the association between a ticket and the service catalog item and converts it back to a ticket form.

To manually remove a ticket's service value
  1. In Support, access a ticket and set the Service field to an empty value.
  2. Save your change by clicking Submit as and selecting the appropriate status.

articles.name: Announcing upcoming changes to WhatsApp Business messaging pricing
articles.title: Announcing upcoming changes to WhatsApp Business messaging pricing
articles.body:
Meta is changing how it charges for WhatsApp Business messages. These changes affect businesses using WhatsApp as a customer support or engagement channel, including those using WhatsApp through the Zendesk platform.

This article contains the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • Will I be affected?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

Since November 2024, non-template messages sent by your business within a 24-hour customer service window have been free. These are messages sent by agents, bots, or automation flows in response to a customer-initiated WhatsApp message.

A customer service window opens when a customer messages your business and remains open for 24 hours after the customer’s most recent message. Starting October 1, 2026, Meta will charge per message for non-template replies sent during this window.

Utility template messages sent within an open customer service window are also currently free. Starting October 1, 2026, these messages will also be charged per message. Rates vary by country and are expected to be published by Meta on September 1, 2026. We’ll share specific figures when they become available.

Meta's messaging fees and your Zendesk account fees are separate. The changes announced by Meta affect Meta's charges. Contact your account manager to understand how Meta messaging costs flow through your specific commercial arrangement with Zendesk.

The following items remain unchanged:

  • Inbound messages from customers to your business remain free
  • The pricing structure for marketing template messages remains unchanged
  • The 72-hour free window for messages following an ad click-to-WhatsApp entry point remains in place
  • Volume-based discounts for utility and authentication messages remain available. The more messages you send, the lower your per-message rate.

Will I be affected?

You are likely to see a meaningful cost change if your WhatsApp setup includes any of the following:

  • Automated chatbots or AI-driven flows that send high volumes of replies to customer messages
  • Automation that sends utility template messages within active customer service windows
  • High-volume WhatsApp support operations where agents respond to large numbers of inbound customer messages

If your WhatsApp usage is primarily low-volume or you are using WhatsApp mainly for outbound marketing templates, the impact will be lower.

Meta Business Agent is Meta's AI product, separate from the AI capabilities available through Zendesk. If your business is using Meta Business Agent, a separate token-based pricing model applies from August 1, 2026. If you are using AI-driven support through Zendesk, this does not apply to you.

What do I need to do?

The following steps will help you get ready for the upcoming price changes:

  1. Review how many service messages and in-window utility templates your business sends per month. This will help you estimate the impact of the change. Your account team can help with this if needed.
    Meta's WhatsApp Manager shows message volume broken down by category (service, utility, marketing), which can help you establish a baseline before October 1, 2026, and track impact afterward. How you access it depends on your setup. If you set up WhatsApp via Zendesk's embedded signup flow, you already have direct access through your own Meta Business Portfolio. If your WhatsApp number was set up before embedded signup was introduced, you can migrate to gain full access. If you are unsure which setup applies to you, your account manager can help clarify.
  2. Meta may reclassify templates between categories (utility vs. marketing). A template reclassified as marketing will be charged at a higher rate. Review your existing utility templates before October 1, 2026, to ensure they are correctly categorized and contain no promotional content.
  3. Utility template messages sent within an open customer service window are currently free. While that exemption ends on October 1, 2026, structuring your automation to reply within active service windows will result in lower costs than sending the same messages outside a window.

If you have questions about how these changes apply to your specific setup, or if you would like help modeling the potential cost impact for your business, contact your Zendesk account manager or customer success manager.

Management

AI Agents

Web Crawler

articles.name: Service Incident - August 4, 2026 - Support | Pod 26 - Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error
articles.title: Service Incident - August 4, 2026 - Support | Pod 26 - Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error
articles.body:
Summary

On August 4, 2026, from 23:34 UTC to 00:28 UTC on August 5, 2026, Zendesk Support customers on Pod 26 experienced an inability to load Z2, receiving 503 errors until service was restored and they refreshed the page.

Timeline

August 5, 2026 00:09 UTC | August 4, 2026 5:09 PM PT

We are aware of an issue affecting Pod 26 in Zendesk Support that is preventing impacted customers and internal advocates from accessing the service. Our engineering team is currently investigating, and we will provide an update in 30 minutes. Thank you for your patience and understanding.

August 5, 2026 00:32 UTC | August 4, 2026 5:32 PM PT

We are happy to inform you that the issue affecting Pod 26 in Zendesk Support, which temporarily prevented impacted customers and internal advocates from accessing the service, has now been resolved. Thank you for your patience and understanding.

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was triggered by the deployment of a new release before all necessary pre-deployment checks had been completed. An issue with our documentation process meant that some important resources weren’t published as planned, leading to temporary service startup problems on one of our systems, which resulted in 503 errors. We are taking steps to ensure this does not happen again.

Resolution

To fix this issue, we first reverted the Lotus deployment to quickly restore service to Z2 on Pod 26. We also removed version 30400 from our main release channel to ensure that this issue does not occur again.

Remediation Items

  1. Implement a validation check to confirm that all required assets and startup processes perform as expected before any deployment.
  2. Enforce that deployments are only initiated after all pre-launch tests have been successfully completed.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: Workflow: Capture a customer’s name and email in an AI agent and sync it to Zendesk tickets
articles.title: Workflow: Capture a customer’s name and email in an AI agent and sync it to Zendesk tickets
articles.body:
AI agents can collect a customer's name and email during a messaging conversation and pass that information to Zendesk when a ticket is created. This is useful when customers start a conversation as anonymous users and you want the resulting ticket to include their details.

This article provides two workflow options:

  • Collect customer details with a customer message block
  • Collect customer details with a form in an AI agent message

In both workflows, you use an Update user action to write the customer's name and email to the Sunshine Conversations user profile before the ticket is created.

Before you start

Before setting up this workflow, make sure that:

  • You're using an AI agent with messaging
  • You have permission to create or edit AI agent flows and actions
  • You understand your account's messaging email identity settings

If you want to associate messaging users with existing Zendesk users before the conversation starts, you also need end-user authentication for messaging using JWT, which requires developer implementation.

Option 1: Use a customer message block

Step 1: Add message blocks to collect the customer's name and email

Add customer message blocks in the flow before the escalation step. Use one block to ask for the customer's name and another to ask for the customer's email address.

Configure each block to save the customer response as a parameter so you can reuse the values later in the flow.

Example:

  • Ask for the customer's name and save it to a parameter such as name
  • Ask for the customer's email address and save it to a parameter such as email

After the values are collected, reference them in later blocks using the parameter format:

  • {{name}}
  • {{email}}

Step 2: Pass the saved values during escalation

When the flow reaches the escalation path or a specific downstream block, create an action and pass the saved parameter values using the parameter formats {{name}} and {{email}}.

Using the double angle bracket {{}} format ensures the stored parameter values are passed correctly.

Option 2: Use a form in an AI agent message

Step 1: Add a form to the AI agent message

Create or select a form template that collects the customer's name and email, then add that form to your AI agent message.

Add the form template to connect it to the relevant flow or escalation path.

Step 2: Verify the parameter names

Then run a test conversation and review the session data to confirm the exact parameter names created by the form. Check the conversation log for the test conversation and review the session parameters ensuring they are set from the template form.

Step 3: Create an Update user action

Create an action for Sunshine Conversations that updates the user profile.

Map the form's saved parameter values to these user fields:

  • givenName = {{name}}
  • email = {{customerEmail}}

The parameter names in the action must exactly match the ones saved by the form.

Step 4: Add the action with the Escalation

Add the Update user action in the escalation block or in the relevant AI agent configuration so it runs before the ticket is created.

This links the collected form details to the Sunshine Conversations user profile before the ticket is generated.

Understand how email identity settings affect the ticket requester

Whether the collected email appears on the Zendesk ticket depends on your messaging email identity settings.

  • If your account allows unverified emails, the email collected by the AI agent can be added as a user identity and used as the ticket requester
  • If your account allows only verified emails, the collected email won't be used as a trusted identity unless the user is authenticated and the email is verified
  • In unauthenticated conversations where only verified emails are allowed, the ticket may appear as a conversation with a web user instead of showing the collected email address

To learn more about email identities see Understanding and setting up end-user authentication for messaging.

If you want to identify customers against existing user profiles before the conversation starts, use JWT-based end-user authentication for messaging. This requires developer implementation or help from Zendesk Professional Services.

articles.name: Service Incident - July 31, 2026 - AI Agents | All Pods - AI Agents Advanced dashboard accessibility issues
articles.title: Service Incident - July 31, 2026 - AI Agents | All Pods - AI Agents Advanced dashboard accessibility issues
articles.body:
Summary

Between July 31, 2026, 01:15 UTC and August 4, 2026, 09:11 UTC, some customers with Employee Service Suite accounts and sandboxes experienced an issue that unexpectedly removed their Ultimate (AI Agents Advanced) entitlement. As a result, affected customers were temporarily unable to access AI Agents Advanced until the issue was resolved and access was restored.

Timeline

August 3, 2026 6:34 UTC | August 2, 2026 11:34 PM PT

We are investigating an issue where a small number of accounts lost access to AI Agents (Ultimate) on Friday, July 31st at approximately 1:20 AM UTC due to a provisioning process error during an Employee Service Suite update. The affected product is AI Agents Advanced. We are working to restore the access in of the known affected accounts in priority and are implementing safeguards to prevent this from happening again. We continue to investigate the full scope of impact and will provide further updates as soon as it becomes available.

August 3, 2026 11:38 UTC | August 3, 2026 4:38 AM PT

We have successfully resolved the issue affecting AI Agents access. All identified accounts have had their access restored. The AI Agents service is now fully operational for all affected customers.

August 4, 2026 9:30 UTC | August 4, 2026 2:30 AM PT (Issue recurrence for some accounts)

We’ve identified additional accounts that lost access to AI Agents as part of the provisioning issue reported earlier. Our engineering team has completed work to restore access for these accounts, and all identified affected accounts should now have their AI Agents access restored.
We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience while we worked to resolve this issue.

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by an incomplete Unleash provisioning and exclusion list used during the Employee Service Suite backfill. Consequently, eligible accounts that should have been excluded were inadvertently processed, resulting in the unintended cancellation of Ultimate (AI Agents Advanced) entitlements.

Resolution

To resolve the issue, the Account Service and Unleash teams restored Ultimate access for all identified affected accounts. They also updated the exclusion list to include impacted and at-risk accounts, preventing unintended entitlement removals during future billing events and synchronization processes. Additionally, accounts that had been incorrectly included in the rollout were removed from the rollout scope to prevent recurrence.

Remediation Items

  1. Share a validated list of all affected accounts with stakeholders before starting any corrective updates.
  2. Require peer review and cross-team approval before performing account removals.
  3. Include the Advocates Team in early communications for visibility into planned changes.
  4. Align with all relevant teams on the rollout plan before executing corrective actions.
  5. Investigate the omission of subscribed accounts from the update process and implement safeguards to prevent similar gaps in future rollouts.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

Issue symptoms

When I make changes to a report included on a dashboard, the new dashboard builder sometimes doesn't automatically enable the Publish button.

How can I fix this issue?

articles.name: Using live call transcripts in Zendesk Talk
articles.title: Using live call transcripts in Zendesk Talk
articles.body:
You can use the transcript to review what has been said and search for details to check information during the call without interrupting the conversation. You can also use real-time suggestions during the call, seeUsing real-time AI suggestions for voice calls.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus

Summary: ◀▼

Live call transcription gives you a real-time text transcript during voice calls, with speaker labels, timestamps, and auto-scrolling updates. You can review what’s been said, search for keywords or phrases, switch transcription language during the call, and check details without interrupting the customer. It also supports multilingual transcription for common languages.

Zendesk Suite customers must also have the Copilot add-on to use this feature.
If your admin has turned on live call transcription, you have access to a real-time text version of a voice call while the conversation is in progress. The transcript shows speaker labels (Agent or Customer), timestamps from the start of the call, and automatically scrolls to show the most recent conversation.

You can use the transcript to review what has been said and search for details to check information during the call without interrupting the conversation. You can also use real-time suggestions during the call, see Using real-time AI suggestions for voice calls.

To use live transcripts during an ongoing call

  1. In the ticket call controls, click Show transcript ().

    The transcript panel opens in the ticket, below the controls, showing the most recent part of the conversation and updates automatically as the conversation continues.

  2. Click the expand icon (v) in the upper-right corner of the transcript panel to access the whole conversation.

    The transcript auto-scrolls to show the latest conversation.
  3. (Optional) Scroll up and down to review the whole conversation.
  4. (Optional) Click Scroll to latest at the bottom of the panel to access the current conversation.

  5. To find a specific topic, search in the upper-right corner of the transcript panel and enter a keyword or phrase.

    It's a case-insensitive search that supports partial matches. This allows you to jump to relevant parts of the conversation and check specific details. For example, information about an "account", "order" or "error message".

    The transcript highlights all instances of the search term. If there are multiple matches, use the arrows to move between matches.

  6. (Optional) In the language menu, select the language you want to use for transcription.

    The transcript language defaults to your Zendesk profile language. You can change the language during an active call to match the language the customer is speaking. The transcript uses the new language for ongoing transcription. Previously transcribed text is not retranscribed.

    You can also select the multilingual language option to seamlessly switch between the following languages only: English, Spanish, French, German, Hindi, Russian, Portuguese, Japanese, Italian, and Dutch.

  7. Click Hide transcript () to close the transcript panel.

    Ending the call also closes the transcript panel.

articles.name: Release notes through 2026-07-31
articles.title: Release notes through 2026-07-31
articles.body:
See the What's New section for an overview of what was released last month.

This week's release notes include:

  • Admin Center
  • Copilot
  • Voice
  • Contact Center
  • Knowledge
  • Mobile SDK's
  • Apps and integrations
  • Products with no updates this week

Admin Center

New:

  • As of July 28, API tokens unused for more than 30 days auto-deactivate. Tokens already deactivated for more than 60 days are deleted. New accounts can't create or use API tokens. 
  • Enhanced session security is rolled out to all accounts as of July 28. See Understanding Zendesk session time.

Copilot

New:

  • Auto assist can now access articles with user segment "Visible to everyone" in Knowledge help centers that require a sign-in. To allow that, go to Admin Center > AI > Auto assist > Manage permissions > Internal content and select Visible to everyone from the dropdown.
  • The agent workspace list of topics (topic in ticket header and left side field) only shows active topics.

Voice

New:

  • Released the ability to view live transcripts in agent workspace. Rollout started on July 29th and will end on August 7th. For more information, see Using live call transcripts in Zendesk Talk and setup instructions.

Contact Center

New:

  • Agents using native Contact Center can now see real-time agent status, availability, and queue information before transferring a call, helping them choose the right transfer target and set better expectations for queue wait times. See Transferring calls.
  • Agents can now view real-time call transcripts with speaker identification, searchable text, and timestamps during active calls. Live transcription is available for Contact Center customers using Amazon Contact Lens. See Using live transcripts.

Fixed:

  • We've fixed the following for agent settings:
    • The "Must include area code" validation was defaulting to the US country code when no country code is selected.
    • The desktop phone's empty state was showing a US flag instead of a globe icon, now corrected to the globe icon.
    • The phone type selector was displaying only "Softphone" for the default option, instead of "Softphone (Default)". It now shows "Softphone (Default)" to distinguish it from a non-default softphone selection.
    • The "Leave without saving" error only triggered when navigating to another settings tab, not when closing the tab; this now triggers in both cases.

Knowledge

Knowledge creation and editing

New:

  • Callouts, tabs, and accordions now render fully styled in the article preview inside the agent ticket interface, so agents see the same formatting that readers see in the help center. See:
    • Using tabs to group content in the article editor
    • Using accordions to create expandable and collapsible sections in the article editor
    • Using callouts to highlight content in the article editor

Fixed:

  • Fixed an issue where the article editor did not show the most recent content for articles managed through the API
  • Fixed an issue where agents were sent into a redirect loop when opening Support from the product tray on a host-mapped help center belonging to a secondary brand.


Help Center

New:

  • Copenhagen theme: The Help Center API now supports creating and deleting user subscriptions, so you can follow and unfollow a user programmatically instead of only through the help center UI.

Fixed:

  • Lisbon theme: Fixed an issue where articles the AI agent referenced in a conversation would not open for accounts using Essential AI Agent 
  • Articles containing a dynamic content placeholder that no longer resolves now render instead of returning an error.

Web Crawler

New:
  • You can now create up to 50 web crawlers per account, up from the previous limit of 20. This allows you to sync and index content from more external sources without needing workarounds.
Fixed:
  • Fixed an issue where web crawlers would fail with "Page fetch failed" errors when the URL extraction service was temporarily unavailable, preventing content from being incorrectly purged during transient service issues.

Mobile SDK's

New:

  • The SDK is now fully compatible with Android 17, aligning with the latest updates and platform requirements from Google.
  • Following a change introduced in Android Gradle Plugin 9.0, applications integrating the SDK must now use the same or a higher compile SDK version. This release requires compileSdk 37. This requirement does not affect the consuming app’s target SDK version. Learn more in the AGP 9.0 release notes.

articles.name: Troubleshooting two-factor authentication (2FA) issues for team members
articles.title: Troubleshooting two-factor authentication (2FA) issues for team members
articles.body:
When a team member signs in for the first time after the two-factor authentication requirement is turned on, they choose how to receive their verification codes. If they set up an authenticator app as their preferred two-factor authentication method, Zendesk Support will not send codes by email or SMS. In that case, they must enter the code generated by the authenticator app.

If they lose access to that app, they cannot sign in with email or SMS unless they later change their two-factor authentication method from their profile settings after regaining access.

To resolve this issue, select an option below:

If the team member uses an authenticator app

  1. Confirm which two-factor authentication method the team member selected when they first signed in
  2. If they selected an authenticator app, ask them to open that app and enter the current verification code
  3. Let them know that email or SMS codes will not be sent while the authenticator app is set as their preferred method

If the team member is locked out of their authenticator app

  1. Ask an admin to generate a temporary recovery code for the team member
  2. The team member can use that recovery code to sign in
  3. For detailed admin steps, See Getting recovery codes for team members locked out of their accounts

If the team member wants to change their two-factor authentication method

  1. After signing in, go to the user profile page
  2. Under Security settings > Two-Factor Authentication, select Manage to update the authentication preferences
  3. For the Preferred method, select Edit to switch from the authenticator app to another supported method, such as email or SMS, if available in the account configuration
  4. Save the changes and use the newly selected method the next time you sign in

Additional notes

  • The delivery method depends on the option the team member originally configured
  • Not receiving an email or SMS code does not always indicate a delivery issue
  • If an authenticator app is configured, the verification code must come from that app
  • An admin may need to assist with account recovery if the team member no longer has access to their device or app

Additional resources

  • Using two-factor authentication to sign in to Zendesk Support

articles.title: Can I use Segments with agentic AI agents for email?
articles.body:
Question

Can I use Segments with agentic AI agents for email? Segments are missing from my procedures. I do not see or find Segments under my Procedure. How and where can I add Segments?

Answer

Yes, you can use segments with email AI agents to target specific audiences.

  • However, Segments do not exist yet within your Procedure. For instance, you cannot use a segment inside a procedure to build a conditional branch.

Instead, you can target the expected audience with a segment by editing your use case directly:

  2. On the Edit use case details pop-up, use the Segments field > Save

articles.name: Why do short agent activities display without full ticket details in real time?
articles.title: Why do short agent activities display without full ticket details in real time?
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

In Zendesk Workforce Management (WFM), short agent activity displays in real time without complete ticket data. These agent activities only last 1 to 30 seconds.

Resolution steps

Agent activities lasting between 1 and 30 seconds may occasionally appear without fully enriched ticket details. 

Cause

This issue arises because Zendesk WFM captures agent activity events, such as ticket updates, almost instantly from the time tracker. However, ticket metadata, including workstream assignment, tags, or status, is captured periodically from Zendesk services, which introduces a short and predictable delay.

When an agent’s action is extremely brief, Zendesk WFM may record the event before it retrieves the ticket metadata, which results in:

  • Incomplete enrichment: Some activities temporarily lack full ticket context, such as a missed workstream assignment
  • Apparent discrepancies: On-screen reports may show a brief misalignment between activity duration and ticket details, even though no data is lost

Zendesk WFM records every event thoroughly and later matches it with its ticket details. The result is a complete, accurate dataset, even if very short activities initially display without full enrichment.

Workarounds and recommendations

Zendesk recommends these approaches:

  • Data recalculation: If you observe discrepancies in activity enrichment, reach out to Zendesk customer support to request a recalculation on stored data
  • Manual updates: For cases where data appears outdated, update tickets manually to ensure workstreams and reports reflect the correct details

For more information, see: About the Agent activity page.

articles.name: Sometimes line-breaks aren’t included when I apply macros
articles.title: Sometimes line-breaks aren’t included when I apply macros
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

At times, line breaks and spaces don't appear when I use a macro. Sometimes the text formatting changes, and the pre-defined text or canned response removes line breaks and spaces. Occasionally, when I apply a macro, the line breaks and spaces don’t show up properly. I don't want my snippet or template to change in ticket responses to customers.

Resolution steps

Copy and pasted content

It's possible you copied content from another source and pasted it into your macro. This action results in incorrect formats in Zendesk.

Follow these steps instead:

  1. Recreate your macro from scratch, don't copy and paste any content

  2. Refresh your ticket page > click Apply macro and retry

Comment placeholders

In addition, using comment placeholders in macros can be inconsistent due to a known limitation in the following events:

  • When applied to a single ticket
  • When applied while bulk-editing a ticket
  • When applied while referencing a placeholder for multi-line or custom text fields

articles.name: Service Incident - July 23, 2026 - Support | Multiple Pods - [Jira v1] Field Sync Not Transmitting
articles.title: Service Incident - July 23, 2026 - Support | Multiple Pods - [Jira v1] Field Sync Not Transmitting
articles.body:
Summary

On July 23, 2026 from 20:42 UTC to 21:31 UTC , some customers using the Jira v1 integration experienced an issue where updates made in Jira did not appear in their linked Zendesk tickets. Other parts of the integration continued to work, but field updates were not completing as expected.
 

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by a recent platform upgrade in the Jira integration service. During the update, an internal component it relied on was no longer available, which caused background tasks to stop completing properly. As a result, field updates were left unfinished. Because the issue happened behind the scenes, it did not produce clear signs of failure, which made it look like the updates were just stuck.
 

Resolution

To fix this issue, we returned the Jira integration service to the previous version that was working as expected. This restored normal processing and allowed updates to complete again. 
 

Remediation Items

To reduce the likelihood of this happening again, we are taking steps including:

  1. Improve alerting for silent job failures
    Add monitoring that detects when background jobs are failing without producing explicit errors or queue growth.

  2. Restore and strengthen integration smoke tests
    Re-enable Jira integration smoke tests with valid test accounts so field-sync failures are caught before production release.

  3. Add safer dependency upgrade checks
    Improve validation for framework upgrades to detect when removed methods or incompatible instrumentation could affect job processing.

  4. Enhance observability for field sync processing
    Add clearer metrics and logs for job pickup, completion, and failure states so stuck syncs can be identified sooner.

  5. Review SLO/SLI coverage for field sync behavior
    Ensure current reliability measurements capture silent failures, not just queue size or explicit error conditions.
     

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.title: Service Incident - July 24, 2026 - Support | Multiple Pods - Customers experiencing server errors when trying to access their Zendesk instances
articles.body:
Summary

On July 24, 2026, between 10:45 UTC and 11:12 UTC, Premier customers across several pods experienced intermittent server errors, which caused occasional difficulties accessing Zendesk Support and Ticketing services.

Timeline

July 24, 2026 11:34 UTC | July 24, 2026 4:34 AM PT

We’re currently investigating an issue that is preventing some customers from accessing Zendesk. Our engineering team is actively working on it, and we’ll share an update as soon as we have more information.

July 24, 2026 13:07 UTC | July 24, 2026 6:07 AM PT

The issue affecting access to Zendesk has now been fully resolved. Customers should once again be able to access the platform normally. We appreciate your patience and understanding while our engineering team investigated and resolved this matter.

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by a network routing failure in our web services partner's US West region, which disrupted connectivity to our infrastructure. This prevented reliable access for customers, leading to increased timeouts and access errors.

Resolution

The issue was resolved by monitoring the network connectivity while our web services partner stabilized their routing in the US West region. Customer access was confirmed to have recovered across all affected areas before transitioning the incident into monitoring and eventual closure.

Remediation Items

  1. Obtain and document a detailed explanation from the content delivery partner about the root cause of the incident.
  2. Review and update the incident report timeline to accurately reflect the observed recovery period.

articles.name: Release notes through 2026-07-24

articles.body:

This week's release notes include:

  • Voice
  • Contact Center
  • Apps and integrations

Admin Center

New:

  • Admins on Enterprise plans will see a new permission option called "Manage Zendesk Support apps" when creating or editing custom roles. This permission appears under the Channels section of the custom role configuration page.
  • Admin Center now shows proactive reminders 5 minutes and 1 minute before your session reaches its maximum duration and you're signed out. Once signed out, the sign-in page will display that it was due to the maximum duration being met. 

Fixed:

  • Notifications for API tokens that will be automatically deactivated or deleted starting July 28 were sent on July 23, and again on July 27. 

Voice

New:

  • Released the ability to auto-accept calls on PSTN lines. Rollout started on July 20 and will end on July 29.

Fixed:

  • The Voice API in Messaging was updated and is now compatible with the Help Center authentication. Before, if the option "Turn on help center authentication" was enabled, the messaging widget would throw a 422 error when using Voice. Following the deployment, we also fixed a CORS issue where the authentication would fail if the widget was hosted on an external (non-Zendesk) domain. 
  • Fixed a bug where the agent ringtone configuration appeared in other agents' profiles, falsely implying one agent could change another's ringtone. In reality, agents can only modify their own ringtone. 
  • Fixed a bug in which the custom ringtone would continue to ring if the agent changed their status while the call was ringing. 

Contact Center

New:

  • When using the channel switcher to place an outbound call from a ticket, if you use the “Enter phone number” option, the call will be linked to the ticket. The agent can clear the linkage if needed.
  • Agents are now able to download logs to troubleshoot issues, with visibility into agent activity, state changes, API calls, warnings, and errors.

  • Added support for Jabra headset controls, allowing users to answer, mute, unmute, and end calls directly from supported headset buttons while keeping call and availability states in sync with Agent Workspace.

Contact Center app

Contact Center app

  • If an agent missed an inbound call and was auto-set to Unavailable, switching back to Available could leave the call console in a broken state. This update restores normal call flow and console behavior so agents can continue handling calls without needing to refresh or logout and login.

Apps and integrations

New:

Mobile SDK's

Android

Breaking Change Notice: The next major version of the Android SDK will require a minimum API level of 24 (Android 7.0). This update is necessary to support the latest Compose BOM requirements.

New:

  • End users can now upload file attachments from within conversation extension web views using the native file picker.
  • End users can now download a transcript of their conversation directly from the conversation screen. See How to enable download transcripts.

Fixed:

  • Fixed an issue where the conversation header subtitle could briefly appear while the conversation was loading or being transferred to an agent or bot.
  • Fixed an issue where the typing indicator did not display the agent's name while they were typing.
  • Fixed an issue where shorthand color values (such as #fff or #000) from theme settings were not applied correctly and fell back to the default color.
  • Fixed a regression where calling the NewConversation API opened an existing conversation instead of creating a new one.
  • Updated the SDK to Kotlin 2.2.21 to support Kotlin versions 2.1 through 2.3. Compatibility for version 2.0.x is now deprecated. This update ensures compatibility for customer applications built on recent Kotlin releases.

iOS

New:

  • The SDK now requires a minimum deployment target of iOS 16. Make sure your app targets iOS 16 or later before updating.

Fixed:

  • Fixed an issue where deep links to older conversations could fail to open because the cache was validated too early.
  • Fixed an issue where a cached session was not cleared on expired-JWT logout when switching between users.
  • Fixed an issue where buttons containing no text were not visible.
  • Fixed a VoiceOver accessibility issue so the "New" messages divider is now correctly announced.
  • Fixed an issue so file label text now respects the device's accessibility text size settings.

App Marketplace

New:
  • Problem Portfolio (Support)
    • Problem Portfolio helps you manage problem tickets and their linked incidents from a single dashboard.  A navbar dashboard lists every active Problem with the count of linked Incidents, the age of the oldest Incident, and a severity score computed from impact. Filter by assignee, priority, tag, or any existing custom field — and group Problems by any dimension you choose. Drill into a Problem to see all linked Incidents. Multi-select and bulk-solve, bulk-tag, or bulk-reassign up to 100 Incidents at a time with rate-limit-aware chunking.
  • Access Monitor (Support) (paid)
    • Access Monitor helps you see who opens sensitive Zendesk tickets and logs it automatically.  Set rules on ticket tags, agent roles, or non-assignee views. When a rule matches, Access Monitor can do things like add a short private internal note to the ticket, apply a tag, log the view in a dedicated access monitor, track last viewer, last view time, and running view count, or add specified agents as ticket followers so they are notified.
  • Mello Claims (Support)
    • Mello is a freight audit and claims platform that helps shippers and logistics teams recover money lost to carrier errors. Mello automatically audits parcel and freight invoices for overcharges and streamlines the filing and tracking of damage, loss, and shortage claims across carriers — turning a slow, manual recovery process into an automated one. Mello Claims brings that recovery workflow directly into Zendesk Support. When a customer contacts your team about a damaged, lost, or delayed shipment, your agents can file a Mello claim without ever leaving the ticket.
  • Hide.fy (Support) (paid)
    • HIde.fy gives you instant, fine-grained control over what each agent sees in Zendesk. No code. No workarounds. Rules apply in real time, directly inside Zendesk Support. Hide.fy lets you define exactly what each agent, group, or brand sees — and everything else disappears. Automatically. Rules are built visually in a central dashboard and take effect immediately — no deploys, no configuration files, no developer required.
  • Skip.ly (Support) (paid)

  • Enreach Omnichannel (Support)

articles.title: Using ServiceNow actions in action flows
articles.body:
Before you can include external actions in your action flows, you must connect the action builder to the external system.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Team, Professional, or Enterprise

Summary: ◀▼

You can connect action flows to ServiceNow to automate creating, updating, searching, and looking up incidents, cases, and users. Use OAuth with a dedicated service account for secure integration. This connection lets you manage ITSM incidents and customer service cases directly within your workflows, improving collaboration and data accuracy across platforms.

By connecting the action builder to external systems, such as ServiceNow, admins can integrate Zendesk with external systems in automated workflows, improving collaboration and maintaining a seamless experience across multiple platforms.
Note: The steps associated with external systems in action flows are referred to collectively as external actions.
This article contains the following topics:
  • Connecting ServiceNow to action builder
  • Using ServiceNow actions in action flows

Connecting ServiceNow to action builder

Before you can include external actions in your action flows, you must connect the action builder to the external system.

When connecting to external systems for use in action flows, the following best practices are recommended:
  • All external actions performed by an action flow are attributed to the user who connected the external system. Therefore, it's a best practice to use a dedicated service account rather than personal credentials when connecting to each external system.
  • All integrations request access to necessary scopes. However, it's important that you review and validate the scopes before authorizing the connection to the external system.
  • When managing credentials for API key-based tools, such as OpenAI, it's best to store keys in a secure vault or credential manager.

To set up OAuth in ServiceNow

Before connecting, you must register an OAuth application in ServiceNow.

The ServiceNow connection requires the useraccount OAuth scope, which enables read and write access to ServiceNow user accounts, incidents, cases, and related records. Review the scope carefully before authorizing the connection. This permission allows action flows to create and modify ServiceNow records on your behalf.

  1. Log into your ServiceNow instance as an admin.
  2. Navigate to System OAuth > Application Registry.
  3. Click New > Create an OAuth API endpoint for external clients.
  4. Enter a name for your application (for example, "Zendesk Action Flows").
  5. Set the Redirect URL to the value provided in the Zendesk connection dialog.
  6. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret values.
  7. Save the application registry entry.
To connect action builder to ServiceNow
  1. In Admin Center, click Apps and integrations in the sidebar, then select Actions > Action flows.
  2. Create or edit an action flow.
  3. Open the step sidebar.
  4. Under External actions, click ServiceNow.
  5. Click Connect.
  6. Enter your ServiceNow instance subdomain (for example, "dev12345" from dev12345.service-now.com).
  7. Enter your OAuth Client ID and OAuth Client Secret from your ServiceNow application registry.
  8. Follow ServiceNow's prompts to authenticate and complete the connection.
    Note: All external actions performed by an action flow are attributed to the user who connected the external system. Therefore, it is a best practice to use a dedicated service account rather than personal credentials when connecting to each external system.

After you've connected to the system, you'll see an indicator that it's connected and details about the instance you're connected to, as well as the actions available for ServiceNow.

Using ServiceNow actions in action flows

The following ServiceNow actions are available:
  • Create incident
  • Update incident
  • Search incidents
  • Lookup incident
  • Create case
  • Update case
  • Search cases
  • Lookup case
  • Lookup user
  • Search users

Creating an incident

Use the Create incident action to create a new ITSM incident record in ServiceNow. This action dynamically loads all available fields (standard and custom) from your ServiceNow incident table at runtime.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Short Description, Caller

Optional: Dynamic fields loaded from your ServiceNow instance (standard and custom fields)
Output Incident details including sys_id, number, short description, state, priority, assignment information, timestamps, and activity status.

Updating an incident

Use the Update incident action to modify fields and status of an existing ServiceNow incident. This action dynamically loads all available incident fields from your ServiceNow instance.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Sys ID

Optional: Dynamic fields loaded from your ServiceNow instance (standard and custom fields)
Output Updated incident details including sys_id, number, description, state, priority, assignment information, resolution details, and timestamps.

Searching for incidents

Use the Search incidents action to find incidents matching specific filter criteria.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Optional: Number, Short Description, State, Priority, Assignment Group, Assigned To, Caller, Category, Active, Opened At From, Opened At To, Created From, Created To, Limit, Offset, Query

All search filters are optional. Combine multiple filters to narrow results. Use Limit and Offset for pagination.
Output Array of incident objects containing sys_id, number, descriptions, state, priority, assignment details, dates, and activity information, plus total count and pagination flag.

Looking up an incident

Use the Lookup incident action to retrieve a single incident by sys_id or incident number.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Optional: Sys ID, Incident Number, Display Value, Exclude Reference Link

You must provide Sys ID or Incident Number to look up an incident.

Use Display Value to control whether reference fields return sys_ids or display names.
Output Complete incident details including sys_id, number, descriptions, state, priority, urgency, impact, assignment information, caller details, resolution details, timestamps, and SLA information.

Creating a case

Use the Create case action to create a new customer service case in ServiceNow CSM. This action dynamically loads all available fields from your ServiceNow case table.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: If dynamic loading fails, this action requires Short Description, Account, Contact, and State as minimum fields.

Optional: Dynamic fields loaded from your ServiceNow case table.
Output Case details including sys_id, number, short description, state, priority, category, account and contact information, assignment details, and timestamps.

Updating a case

Use the Update case action to modify fields and status of an existing ServiceNow case. This action dynamically loads all available case fields from your ServiceNow instance.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Sys ID

Optional: Dynamic fields loaded from your ServiceNow case table (standard and custom fields)
Output Updated case details including sys_id, number, description, state, priority, assignment information, escalation status, and timestamps.

Searching for cases

Use the Search cases action to find customer service cases matching specific filter criteria.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Optional: Multiple filter fields including case number, description, state, priority, account, contact, assignment details, dates, and pagination controls.

All search filters are optional. Combine multiple filters to narrow results. Use Limit and Offset for pagination.
Output Array of case objects containing sys_id, number, descriptions, state, priority, account and contact information, assignment details, and timestamps, plus total count and pagination flag.

Looking up a case

Use the Lookup case action to retrieve a single case by sys_id or case number.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Optional: Sys ID, Case Number, Display Value, Exclude Reference Link (at least one of Sys ID or Case Number required)

You must provide either Sys ID or Case Number to lookup a case. Use Display Value to control whether reference fields return sys_ids or display names.
Output Complete case details including sys_id, number, descriptions, state, priority, account and contact information, assignment details, resolution information, and timestamps.

Looking up a user

Use the Lookup user action to retrieve a single ServiceNow user by sys_id or email address.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Optional: Sys ID, Email, Display Value, Active (at least one of Sys ID or Case Number required)

You must provide either Sys ID or Email to look up a user. Use the Active filter to return only active users.
Output User details including sys_id, username, first and last name, full name, email, active status, job title, department, manager, phone numbers, timezone, and creation date

Searching for users

Use the Search users action to find ServiceNow users by name, email, username, or department.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs

Optional: Name, Email, Username, Active, Department, Limit, Offset

All search filters are optional and support partial matching (except Username which requires exact match). Use Limit and Offset for pagination.
Output Array of user objects containing sys_id, username, names, email, active status, job title, department, manager, contact information, and timezone, plus total count and pagination flag.

articles.name: Service Incident - July 16, 2026 - Chat | Pod 25 - Ticket creation delays
articles.title: Service Incident - July 16, 2026 - Chat | Pod 25 - Ticket creation delays
articles.body:
Summary

On July 16, 2026 from 03:50 UTC to 05:36 UTC , Chat (Agent Workspace) customers in Pod 25 experienced degraded performance, primarily elevated latency and delays when creating tickets. Messaging was not affected.
 

Timeline

July 16, 2026 5:23 UTC 
We are actively investigating an issue affecting customers in Pod 25, which is causing a degraded experience in Chat within Agent Workspace. Customers may experience delays when creating tickets. The Messaging product should not be affected. Our engineers are actively working to resolve the issue, and we will provide an update as soon as more information becomes available. Thank you for your patience.

July 16, 2026 5:56 UTC
The service has now recovered, and performance returned to normal levels at approximately 5:36 AM UTC. We are continuing to monitor closely for any recurrence and investigating the underlying contributors to help ensure stability and prevent a repeat. Thank you for your patience.
 
July 16, 2026 6:34 UTC 
We’re happy to share that the issue causing degraded Chat performance in Agent Workspace has been resolved, and service is now operating normally again. We’ve also put preventive measures in place to help reduce the likelihood of recurrence while we continue our follow-up investigation. Thank you again for your patience and understanding.
 

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by a sudden surge of high-volume ticket update activity from a single customer account, which led to unexpected load on the database supporting Ticket Log Service in Pod 25. That database load resulted in processing delays that impacted Chat ticket creation in Agent Workspace.
 

Resolution

To fix this issue, we implemented a temporary rate limit on the high-volume traffic pattern to protect overall service stability. After the limit was put in place, database load reduced and service performance returned to normal.
 

Remediation Items

To reduce the likelihood of this happening again, we are taking steps including:

  1. Improving query-level monitoring and alerting so we can detect expensive database query patterns earlier
  2. Reducing unnecessary database work in Ticket Log Service that can amplify load during traffic spikes
  3. Reviewing safeguards (such as targeted throttling) to prevent a single customer’s automation from degrading performance for other customers on the same Pod
     

FOR MORE INFORMATION

articles.name: Service Incident - July 14, 2026 - AI Agents | Multiple Pods - AI Agents Repeating Messages
articles.title: Service Incident - July 14, 2026 - AI Agents | Multiple Pods - AI Agents Repeating Messages
articles.body:
Summary

On July 14, 2026, between 14:40 UTC and 17:00 UTC, some customers experienced AI Agents getting stuck in loops and sending repeated messages in bot conversations. In some cases, this continued even after an end user stopped responding or after a human agent replied.
 

Timeline

July 14, 2026 17:21 UTC 
We are aware of an issue affecting bot conversations causing looped or repeating messages across multiple pods. Our team is investigating and we will provide further updates shortly.
 
July 14, 2026 17:37 UTC 
We have rolled back a recent change which appears to have caused messaging conversations to loop or repeat bot messages, and we are seeing conversation errors drop off. Please let us know if you are still experiencing any issues in conversations.
 
July 14, 2026 18:13 UTC 
We are happy to report that the issue causing repeated and looping messages in bot conversations has been resolved. Thank you for your patience during our investigation.
 

Root Cause Analysis

A change to a cleanup job increased query timeouts to accommodate a growing backlog. Under real production load, the query ran long enough to hold locks on key database tables, blocking the live webhook processing path.

This lock contention resulted in database “lock wait timeout” errors during inbound webhook processing, preventing conversation state from being updated and leading to repeated/looping bot behavior.
 

Resolution

  • We confirmed the issue via logs and reproduction in a test account.
  • We rolled back the cleanup job change.
  • After rollback, conversation processing errors dropped and customer reports indicated the looping/repeating behavior stopped.
     

Remediation Items

We are taking steps to reduce the likelihood of recurrence and improve earlier detection:

  • Query and job improvements: Rework and optimize the cleanup process so it can handle backlog safely without locking behavior that impacts live traffic.
  • Monitoring and alerting: Add/adjust monitoring so we detect job failures, rising lock-wait timeouts, and related error patterns earlier.
  • Operational safeguards: Review rollout safeguards for changes that can affect database performance or locking, especially for background jobs sharing the same database as live request paths.
     

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

You can connect action builder to Microsoft Azure DevOps to automate workflows that create, update, and manage work items, pull requests, projects, and pipelines. Use external actions like creating work items, adding comments, triggering pipeline runs, and retrieving statuses to improve collaboration and streamline task management across platforms. Use a dedicated service account for secure authentication and proper permissions.

By connecting the action builder to external systems, such as Microsoft Azure DevOps, admins can integrate Zendesk with external systems in automated workflows, improving collaboration and maintaining a seamless experience across multiple platforms.
Note: The steps associated with external systems in action flows are referred to collectively as external actions.
This article contains the following topics:
  • Connecting Microsoft Azure DevOps to action builder
  • Using Microsoft Azure DevOps actions in action flows

Connecting Microsoft Azure DevOps to action builder

When connecting to external systems for use in action flows, the following best practices are recommended:
  • All external actions performed by an action flow are attributed to the user who connected the external system. Therefore, it's a best practice to use a dedicated service account rather than personal credentials when connecting to each external system.

  • When managing credentials for API key-based tools, such as OpenAI, it's best to store keys in a secure vault or credential manager.
To connect action builder to Microsoft Azure DevOps
  1. In Admin Center, click Apps and integrations in the sidebar, then select Actions > Action flows.
  2. Create or edit an action flow.
  3. Open the step sidebar.
  4. Under External actions, click Microsoft Azure DevOps.
  5. Click Connect.
  6. Follow Microsoft Azure DevOps's prompts to authenticate and complete the connection.

    The Microsoft Azure DevOps connection uses OAuth 2.0 for secure authentication. You'll be redirected to Microsoft to authorize access to your Azure DevOps organization. The connector automatically handles token refresh when needed.

    Ensure the authenticating user has appropriate permissions in your Azure DevOps organization for the operations you plan to perform through action flows.

    Note: All external actions performed by an action flow are attributed to the user who connected the external system. Therefore, it is a best practice to use a dedicated service account rather than personal credentials when connecting to each external system.

After you've connected to the system, you'll see an indicator that it's connected and details about the instance you're connected to, as well as the actions available for Microsoft Azure DevOps.

Using Microsoft Azure DevOps actions in action flows

The following Microsoft Azure DevOps actions are available:
  • Create work item
  • Update work item
  • Lookup work item
  • Add comment to work item
  • List work items
  • Create pull request
  • Update pull request
  • Lookup pull request
  • List pull requests
  • Lookup project
  • List projects
  • List pipelines
  • Trigger pipeline run
  • Get pipeline status
  • List pipeline runs

Creating a work item

Use the Create work item action to create a new work item in an Azure DevOps project.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project, Work item type, Title

The Work item type field dynamically populates based on your project configuration and may include Bug, Task, User Story, Epic, Feature, or custom types.

Optional: Description, Assigned to, State, Priority, Tags, Area path, Iteration path, Repro steps, Acceptance criteria, Story points, Original estimate, Remaining work, Severity, Activity, Parent ID, Reason

Optional fields vary by work item type (for example, Repro steps for Bugs, Acceptance criteria for User Stories).
Output Work item object including id, rev, work_item_type, title, description, state, assigned_to, created_date, changed_date, url, and all field details.

Updating a work item

Use the Update work item action to modify an existing work item's fields.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Work item ID

Optional: Project, Title, Description, Assigned to, State, Priority, Tags, Reason, Area path, Iteration path, Remaining work, Completed work, Story points, Severity, Activity

Only provided fields are changed. Existing values for fields you don't specify remain unchanged.

Selecting a Project enables state, area path, and iteration path options specific to that project.
Output Updated work item object including id, rev, work_item_type, title, changed_date, url, and all updated field details.

Looking up a work item

Use the Lookup work item action to retrieve detailed information about a specific work item by its ID.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Work item ID

Optional: Expand relations, Expand comments

Set Expand relations to Yes to include parent, child, and related work items as well as links and attachments.

Set Expand comments to Yes to include all comments and discussion history.
Output Work item object including all fields, with optional parent, children, related_work_items, attachments, and comments array.

Adding a comment to a work item

Use the Add comment to work item action to post a comment on a work item.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project, Work item ID, Comment text
Output Comment object including comment_id, work_item_id, text, created_by, created_date, modified_date, url, and comment_version.

Listing work items

Use the List work items action to search for work items using WIQL (Work Item Query Language) or filter fields.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project

Optional: Query, Title contains, Work item type, State, Assigned to, Tags contain, Area path, Max results, Sort field, Sort order

You can use the Query field to write custom WIQL queries for advanced filtering, or leave it blank to use the simple filter fields below.

Max results defaults to 50 and cannot exceed 200.

Sort field accepts Changed Date, Created Date, Title, or Priority.
Output Results array of work items with total_count and has_more pagination flag.

Creating a pull request

Use the Create pull request action to create a new pull request in a Git repository.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project, Repository, Source branch, Target branch, Title

Optional: Description, Reviewers, Work item IDs, Is draft, Auto complete, Labels, Merge strategy, Delete source branch

Branch names should use the format feature/branch-name or refs/heads/feature/branch-name.

Reviewers should be comma-separated email addresses.

Work item IDs should be comma-separated numeric IDs.

Set Is draft to Yes to create as a draft pull request.
Output Pull request object including pull_request_id, title, description, status, created_date, created_by, repository, source_branch, target_branch, reviewers array, work_item_refs array, url, and web_url.

Updating a pull request

Use the Update pull request action to modify an existing pull request.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project, Repository, Pull request ID

Optional: Title, Description, Status, Is draft, Auto complete enabled, Merge strategy

Only provided fields are changed.

Status accepts active, completed, or abandoned.

Set Auto complete enabled to Yes to automatically merge when all policies pass.
Output Updated pull request object including pull_request_id, title, status, merge details, last_merge_commit, closed_date, url, and web_url.

Looking up a pull request

Use the Lookup pull request action to retrieve detailed information about a specific pull request.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project, Repository, Pull request ID

Optional: Include commits, Include work items

Set Include commits to Yes to retrieve all commits included in the pull request.

Set Include work items to Yes to retrieve linked work items.
Output Detailed pull request object including all fields, reviewers array, labels array, optional commits and work_item_refs arrays, completion_options, url, and web_url.

Listing pull requests

Use the List pull requests action to retrieve pull requests from a Git repository.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project, Repository

Optional: Status, Creator ID, Reviewer ID, Source branch, Target branch, Max results, Skip

Status accepts all (default), active, completed, or abandoned.

Max results accepts 1-100 (default: 50).

Use Skip for pagination to skip the first N results.
Output Pull requests array with pull request objects plus pagination details with total_count and has_more flag.

Looking up a project

Use the Lookup project action to retrieve details about a specific Azure DevOps project.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project

Optional: Include capabilities, Include history

Set Include capabilities to Yes to retrieve version control and process template details.

Set Include history to Yes to retrieve project change history.
Output Project object including id, name, description, state, visibility, default_team, url, with optional capabilities and history.

Listing projects

Use the List projects action to retrieve all projects in an organization.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization

Optional: State filter, Continuation token, Max results

State filter accepts All, WellFormed (active projects, default), Deleting, or New.

Max results accepts 1-100 (default: 100).
Output Projects array with project objects including id, name, description, state, visibility, and url, plus total_count and continuation_token.

Listing pipelines

Use the List pipelines action to retrieve build and release pipelines in a project.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project

Optional: Pipeline name, Folder path, Continuation token

Pipeline name supports partial matching. Folder path format is \Production or \CI\Builds.
Output Pipelines array with pipeline objects including id, name, folder, revision, url, and web_url, plus total_count and continuation_token.

Triggering a pipeline run

Use the Trigger pipeline run action to manually trigger a pipeline execution.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Organization, Project, Pipeline ID

Optional: Branch, Variables, Resources repositories, Stages to skip

Branch format is main or refs/heads/feature/branch-name.

Variables should be a JSON object (for example, {"Environment": "Production"}).
Output Run object including run_id, run_number, pipeline details, state, result, created_date, finished_date, url, and web_url.

Getting pipeline run status

Use the Get pipeline run status action to retrieve the status and details of a pipeline run.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables

Output Detailed run object including run_id, run_number, name, state, result, pipeline details, created_date, and finished_date.

State indicates the current status (in progress, completed, canceling, cancelled). Result indicates the outcome (succeeded, failed, canceled, etc.).

Listing pipeline runs

Use the List pipeline runs action to retrieve recent runs for a specific pipeline.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables

Optional: Result filter, State filter, Max results, Continuation token

Result filter accepts all, succeeded, failed, etc. Max results accepts 1-100 (default: 50).
